issue_context.title: ESQL: incorrect optimization rule behavior for different type, same name field STATS usage
issue_context.body:
### Description

For query `FROM sample_data_str, sample_data | eval ip = to_string(client_ip) | STATS count=count(*) BY ip` the output is 

```
     count     |      ip       
---------------+---------------
8              |172.21.3.15    
2              |172.21.0.5     
2              |172.21.2.113   
2              |172.21.2.162   
```

while adding one more `stats` the behavior is unexpected

`FROM sample_data_str, sample_data | eval ip = to_string(client_ip) | STATS count=count(*) BY ip | STATS mc=count(count) BY count`

```
      mc       |     count     
---------------+---------------
6              |1              
2              |4              
```

Enabling TRACE logging there is this transformation that doesn't look like it's doing the right thing:

```
[TRACE][o.e.x.e.o.LogicalPlanOptimizer] [runTask-0] Rule rules.CombineProjections applied
Limit[1000[INTEGER]]                                                                = Limit[1000[INTEGER]]
\_Aggregate[STANDARD,[count{r}#735],[COUNT(count{r}#735) AS mc, count{r}#735]]      = \_Aggregate[STANDARD,[count{r}#735],[COUNT(count{r}#735) AS mc, count{r}#735]]
  \_Aggregate[STANDARD,[ip{r}#732],[COUNT(*[KEYWORD]) AS count, ip{r}#732]]         !   \_Aggregate[STANDARD,[client_ip{f}#741],[COUNT(*[KEYWORD]) AS count, client_ip{f}#741 AS ip]]
    \_Project[[client_ip{f}#740, client_ip{f}#741 AS ip]]                           !     \_EsRelation[sample_data_str,sample_data][client_ip{f}#740, client_ip{f}#741]
      \_EsRelation[sample_data_str,sample_data][client_ip{f}#740, client_ip{f}#741] !
```

The evaluated `ip` disappears and `client_ip` is being used instead. In these two indices, though, `client_ip` has different types (one is `keyword` the other is `ip`) and based on this differentiation the counts in the final result seem legit.
